products.name: Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) with Netskope Private Access — VPN Replacement — Commercial
products.short_description: Replace the VPN with Zero Trust Network Access using Netskope Private Access — publish private apps, grant identity- and posture-based least-privilege access, and reach apps without exposing the network, via a staged cutover. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Replace the VPN — give users least-privilege access to private apps, not the whole network

Legacy VPN hands a user the whole network and is slow, hard to scale, and a favorite attacker on-ramp. This solution replaces it with Zero Trust Network Access using Netskope Private Access — publish individual private applications, grant identity- and posture-based least-privilege access, and reach apps without exposing the network — with a staged coexistence-then-cutover migration off the VPN.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — how ZTNA / Netskope Private Access works, private app publishing, identity- and posture-based access, the difference from VPN, and the coexistence-then-cutover migration.
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Netskope tenant + Private Access, publisher/connector placement, Entra ID identity, the Netskope client, app inventory, a pilot group) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.
  • Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: deploy publishers/connectors, define private apps and access policy, steer pilot users, validate access and posture, run VPN coexistence then cutover, then expand.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — ZTNA-readiness discovery, private-app access validation, an access and usage report, safe remediation of broken app access, and a ZTNA user-assignment group builder.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Users reaching only the private apps they're entitled to — least-privilege, identity- and posture-based access with no network exposure — and the legacy VPN retired, proven on a pilot before you scale.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • NSZTNA-Discovery.ps1 — ZTNA readiness: endpoint posture, current VPN routes/hosts, publisher candidates
    • NSZTNA-Remediation.ps1 — safe fixes for broken ZTNA access (default -WhatIf)
    • NSZTNA-Report.ps1 — access + usage report: who is entitled to which apps (Entra), plus posture
    • NSZTNA-Set-AccessGroupTargeting.ps1 — build/update the Entra entitlement groups for ZTNA access
    • NSZTNA-Validation.ps1 — validate a pilot user/device for ZTNA: client, group, posture, app reach

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
